scope: GH-464 slice 1 and GH-466 registration slice: main-process ipcMain cells for the macOS draw.io first-proof IPC path at Electron 44.4.5. Registration cells (listener array, invoke-handler table) pass; delivery cells stay pending for GH-466 (listeners) and GH-547 (invoke). No renderer transport, native WebKit, product compatibility or whole-family completion claim.

doc_citation.quote:
Listens to `channel`, when a new message arrives `listener` would be called with
`listener(event, args...)`.

cells.test_name: ipc-main.on today: ipcMain.on registers the listener, but no message can arrive: no IpcMainEvent value exists and the listener is never invoked
cells.negative_control: Today: an exported IpcMainEvent value, or any Keld path that invokes the registered listener without an admitted renderer message, makes this mapped current-behaviour case fail. After the GH-466 delivery slice flips it, removing listener dispatch must produce zero callbacks instead of the expected event and arguments.

doc_citation.quote:
Adds a one time `listener` function for the event. This `listener` is invoked
only the next time a message is sent to `channel`, after which it is removed.

cells.test_name: ipc-main.once today: ipcMain.once registers a one-time listener, but no message can arrive: no IpcMainEvent value exists and the listener is never invoked
cells.negative_control: Today: registering the original function instead of EventEmitter's once wrapper, exporting an IpcMainEvent value, or invoking the listener without an admitted message makes this mapped case fail. After GH-466 flips it, replacing once with on must make two admitted messages invoke the callback twice instead of once; a reentrant send must not call the removed listener again.

cells.test_name: ipc-main.remove-listener: removeListener removes exactly one occurrence like off, including a once registration by its original function
cells.negative_control: A removeListener that removes every occurrence, removes nothing, or cannot find a once registration by its original function fails the exact listener-array comparison; replacing it with off's behaviour keeps the case green, which is the cited alias.

cells.test_name: ipc-main.event-emitter: ipcMain is one node:events EventEmitter instance shared by the named and default electron exports
cells.negative_control: Exporting a plain object with hand-written on/once methods, or a different object on the default export, fails the instanceof and identity assertions; the listener-array cells then fail independently.

doc_citation.quote:
Removes the specified `listener` from the listener array for the specified
`channel`.

cells.test_name: ipc-main.off.removes-listener: off removes exactly the given listener from the channel's listener array and leaves the other entries in order
cells.negative_control: An off that clears the whole channel, removes a different listener, or reorders the survivors fails the exact listeners() array comparison before and after the call.

doc_citation.quote: Removes all listeners from the specified `channel`. Removes all listeners from all channels if no channel is specified.

cells.test_name: ipc-main.remove-all-listeners: removeAllListeners(channel) empties only that channel; with no channel an observer child sees every channel emptied
cells.negative_control: A removeAllListeners(channel) that also empties a neighbouring channel fails the in-process count assertion; a no-argument call that leaves any channel, including Electron's internal error listener, non-empty fails the observer child's eventNames census.

cells.test_name: ipc-main.add-listener.alias: addListener appends to the same listener array as on, in registration order with duplicates kept
cells.negative_control: An addListener that deduplicates, prepends, or writes to a table on cannot see fails the exact listeners() array built from interleaved on and addListener calls.

doc_citation.quote: Adds a handler for an `invoke`able IPC.

cells.test_name: ipc-main.handle.registers: handle records one invoke handler per channel and refuses a second with KELD-COMPAT-098 before checking the handler type
cells.negative_control: A handle that records nothing lets the second registration succeed and fails the KELD-COMPAT-098 assertion; checking the handler type before the duplicate makes handle(channel, 42) on an occupied channel raise KELD-COMPAT-099 and fails the ordering assertion.

doc_citation.quote:
This handler will be called whenever a
renderer calls `ipcRenderer.invoke(channel, ...args)`.

cells.test_name: ipc-main.handle.invoked today: ipcMain.handle records the handler, but no renderer invoke can reach it: no IpcMainInvokeEvent value exists and the handler is never called
cells.negative_control: Today: an exported IpcMainInvokeEvent value, or any Keld path that calls the recorded handler without an admitted renderer invoke, makes this mapped case fail. After GH-547 flips it, disconnecting invoke dispatch must leave the handler uncalled instead of returning its value to the caller.

doc_citation.quote: Handles a single `invoke`able IPC message, then removes the listener.

cells.test_name: ipc-main.handle-once today: ipcMain.handleOnce records a single-use handler, but no renderer invoke can reach it: nothing is handled or removed because nothing is sent
cells.negative_control: Today: a handleOnce that records nothing lets a later handle on the same channel succeed and fails the KELD-COMPAT-098 assertion; invoking the wrapper without an admitted invoke fails the zero-call assertion. After GH-547 flips it, a second invoke must find no handler instead of being handled twice.

doc_citation.quote: Removes any handler for `channel`, if present.

cells.test_name: ipc-main.remove-handler: removeHandler clears the channel's handler if present so handle registers again, and is a no-op for an absent channel
cells.negative_control: A removeHandler that leaves the handler in place makes the following handle raise KELD-COMPAT-098; one that throws for an absent channel fails the no-op assertion.
